title: "Static Routes across Three NOSes"

# Static Routes across Three NOSes

The forwarding chapter used loopbacks and two statics each. This chapter adds a host LAN behind each router and a default on the host, which is the shape you actually operate.

Use the same triangle as Three-Router Forwarding. Add one Alpine host on a third data port of each router.

## Learning goals

By the end of this chapter you can:

- Number a LAN on FRR, cEOS, and SR Linux
- Point each host at its router
- Install the two remote LAN routes on each router
- Find which static is missing when one direction fails

## Prefixes

| Router | LAN | Host |
|--------|-----|------|
| r-frr eth3 | 172.16.1.1/24 | h-frr 172.16.1.10 via .1 |
| r-ceos Ethernet3 | 172.16.2.1/24 | h-ceos 172.16.2.10 via .1 |
| r-srl ethernet-1/3 | 172.16.3.1/24 | h-srl 172.16.3.10 via .1 |

Transit links stay 10.1.12.0/30, 10.1.13.0/30, and 10.1.23.0/30.

Each router needs a static for the two LANs it does not own. r-frr:

```text
ip route 172.16.2.0/24 10.1.12.2
ip route 172.16.3.0/24 10.1.13.2
```

r-ceos uses EOS syntax (`ip route 172.16.1.0/24 10.1.12.1`). r-srl uses a next-hop-group per prefix, the same shape as the forwarding chapter.

cEOS Ethernet3 is `no switchport` before the address. SR Linux must bind `ethernet-1/3.0` into `network-instance default`.

## Verify

```bash
docker exec clab-static-h-frr ping -c 2 172.16.2.10
docker exec clab-static-h-frr ping -c 2 172.16.3.10
docker exec clab-static-r-frr vtysh -c "show ip route"
```

### Predict

- h-frr reaches both remote hosts.
- Delete only `172.16.3.0/24` on r-ceos. h-frr still reaches h-srl if the path is r-frr to r-srl direct. h-ceos stops reaching h-srl.
- A missing host default looks like a router failure and is not. Check `ip route` on the host first.

## Drill

Add a floating static on r-frr for 172.16.2.0/24 via r-srl (10.1.13.2) with distance 50, and keep the primary via r-ceos at distance 1. Shut r-ceos Ethernet1. The LAN moves to the long path. Confirm with `traceroute` from h-frr.
